intro_html: Rogan josh is a Kashmiri dish, and the authentic version does something almost no other Indian curry does: it uses no onions and no tomatoes at all. The deep red color comes from Kashmiri chiles, which are more about pigment than punishment. The body comes from yogurt, whisked in slowly so it does not split, and the perfume comes from dried ginger and fennel. It is a short list of ingredients doing very precise work. Each serving runs 659 calories and 54 grams of protein for about $2.50.
cost_closing_html: About $2.50 a serving. This one is priced by its spice cabinet, not its produce, because the recipe skips vegetables entirely. Buy the ginger, fennel and dried chiles once and the next batch costs you a lot less.
shop_smart: Dried chiles, ground ginger and ground fennel together make up more of this batch than the vegetables in most of our recipes. All three are dramatically cheaper in bags from an international grocer than in branded jars, and all three keep for a year in sealed containers.
Greek yogurt is the sauce. Buy the big tub of plain full fat, not the flavored cups, and let it come to room temperature before it goes in the pot so it is less likely to split.
Butter and oil are both here for a reason: the oil takes the heat and the butter carries the flavor. Buy butter in the one pound box rather than sticks sold individually, which run higher per ounce.
This curry has no rice line, so plan for a starch on the side if you want it. A pot of plain rice adds almost nothing to your cost and stretches the batch further.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend them with a little of the soaking liquid into a smooth red paste. That paste is the color and the soul of the dish.
Whisk the greek yogurt with the milk until it is completely smooth and pourable. Cold, thick yogurt is what splits, so take the minute.
Heat the vegetable oil and butter together in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, add the bay leaves, and let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken thighs and sear them, working in batches so the pot stays hot. Return them all to the pot with the minced garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the chile paste, chili powder, ground fennel, ground ginger, ground coriander, ground cumin and salt and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the oil turns red and separates.

Turn the heat to low and add the yogurt mixture a ladle at a time, stirring constantly and letting each addition come together before the next goes in. Rushing this is how you end up with curdled sauce.
Cover and simmer gently 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is glossy, then stir in the garam masala off the heat.
portion_html: Set the pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Fourteen even portions, no arguing about it. Each one carries 659 calories, and reheat this one gently at half power, because a yogurt sauce that boils will break on you.
upsell_html: Kashmiri rogan josh, no onions and no tomatoes, for about $2.50 a serving. This is one of a few hundred recipes on the site. Members get the whole Meal Prep section plus every money lesson, calculator, and tool for $1 a month.

head.description: Chicken rogan josh, the Kashmiri way: no onion or tomato, deep red from dried chiles, thickened with yogurt. 14 meal prep servings at 659 calories, 54g protein, about $2.50.
head.keywords: chicken rogan josh, kashmiri curry, yogurt curry, indian chicken curry, no onion curry, high protein meal prep
steps: Soak and blend the dried chiles into a smooth red paste, and whisk the yogurt with the milk until pourable.
Sear the chicken thighs in oil and butter with bay leaves, in batches.
Add garlic and the chile paste with fennel, ginger, coriander and cumin, and cook until the oil separates and turns red.
Add the yogurt a ladle at a time over low heat, stirring constantly so it does not split.
Cover and simmer 35 to 40 minutes, stir in garam masala off the heat, and portion into 14 containers.
